samples.summary: `sheet-author` codeScope names a directory that does not exist (`packages/frontend/src/app/sheets/**`), so half the surface it explores can never satisfy the gate's citation stage
samples.evidence: personas.json declares `"codeScope": ["packages/sheets/src/**", "packages/frontend/src/app/sheets/**"]`. There is no `packages/frontend/src/app/sheets` directory in the tree — the spreadsheet UI lives in `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/` (sheet-view.tsx, use-object-layer.ts, …), and the toolbar/context-menu code is in `packages/frontend/src/components/`. `isFilingVerdict` step 4 filters verifier `groundedIn` through `citationInScope(citation, charter.codeScope)` (hunt-gate.mjs:428), so any sheet finding a verifier localises to the frontend spreadsheet code is silently dropped as "insufficient or out-of-scope citations". The same wrong glob is also handed to `makeChangedSince` for ledger expiry, so ledger entries keyed on frontend sheet code will never expire. The doc persona has the analogous path correct (`packages/frontend/src/app/docs/**` does exist), which is why this reads as a typo rather than a deliberate narrowing.

samples.summary: The UI verifier is the sole source of citations for the gate, but its prompt never states the persona's `codeScope` or the repo-relative `path:line` format the gate requires
samples.evidence: `uiCitationsOf` makes `groundedIn` the only input to `isFilingVerdict` step 4 (hunt-gate.mjs:428 `citationInScope(…, charter.codeScope)` + the `CITATION` regex). The verifier prompt only says "`groundedIn` must name file:line locations you actually read" — it does not tell the verifier which paths are in scope, nor that a bare `text-editor.ts:44` is not acceptable. The CLI hunter tells its explorer both, explicitly and repeatedly (`charters/contract.md:15` "`packages/cli/src/**`", `charters/crash.md:47` "`packages/cli/src/commands/schema.ts:33`, never `schema.ts:33`"), because that is where its citations come from. With the citation source moved to the verifier and none of that guidance moved with it, the most likely outcome of a live run is every reproduced, confirmed candidate dropping at stage 4 for a reason nothing in the report explains as a formatting problem.

samples.summary: `run --fault` writes a seeded-fault run's fabricated findings into the same report, run.json and novelty ledger as a real hunt, with no marker in any artifact
samples.evidence: `cmdRun` accepts `--fault`, threads it into `runHunt`, and `runHunt` announces it only on stderr (`FAULT INJECTION ACTIVE … this run is a positive control, not a hunt`). Everything downstream is unconditional: `report.md`, `run.json` and `hunt-ui-execution.json` are written to the normal outDir, and `ledgerAdds` records the seeded defect key (e.g. `doc-writer|type|doc.text|contains|A`) as `verdict: "reported"`. That key is generic enough to collide with a genuine ground-A prediction defect, so a control run can permanently suppress a real finding. It also contradicts the design's own stated rule for this feature — page.tsx:80 and harness-engineering.md's Phase 31 say the active fault is published as `data-hunt-harness-fault` precisely so "a seeded run can never be mistaken for a real one when someone reads a report" — yet the report the maintainer actually reads carries no fault field at all. The design doc describes the positive control as being exercised by `verify:hunt:oracles`; the end-to-end `run --fault` path is additional surface with no separation of ledger or output directory.

samples.summary: Seven CLI/environment helpers are copy-pasted verbatim from hunt.mjs; only the report renderer's duplication is justified in the design doc
samples.evidence: `parseArgs`, `fail`, `strArg`, `gitSha`, `repoSlug`, `makeChangedSince` and `loadContext` are byte-for-byte (or near) copies of hunt.mjs:541-613 and hunt.mjs:1268-1302, including the comment-worthy `gh repo view` slug resolution and the ledger-expiry git-log walk. The Phase 31 doc argues only that the REPORT RENDERER is deliberately not shared ("duplicating it costs a little prose and no correctness"); it says nothing about these, and they carry no presentation argument — a change to the slug resolution or to `WAFFLEBASE_HUNT_*` config now has to be made twice. A `hunt-cli-args.mjs`/`hunt-context.mjs` extraction would match the repo's stated reuse expectation and be covered by the existing agent:tests lane.

verdict.reason: Verified directly. personas.json:58-61 declares the sheet-author codeScope as ["packages/sheets/src/**", "packages/frontend/src/app/frontend sheets glob"] — literally "packages/frontend/src/app/sheets/**" — and that directory does not exist: globbing packages/frontend/src/app/s*/** yields settings/, shared/, slides/, spreadsheet/, with the spreadsheet UI at packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/ (sheet-view.tsx, use-object-layer.ts, yorkie-store.ts). Repo docs confirm the canonical path (design-system-unification.md:175, slides/slides.md:102 reference app/spreadsheet); nothing under docs/ references app/sheets. The doc persona's analogous entry (personas.json:20, packages/frontend/src/app/docs/**) does resolve, supporting the typo reading. Mechanism confirmed: isFilingVerdict stage 4 (hunt-gate.mjs:551) requires some citation to pass citationInScope against charter.codeScope (hunt-gate.mjs:428-433), so any verifier groundedIn under app/spreadsheet is dropped as out-of-scope; and hunt-ui.mjs:1005 hands the same globs to makeChangedSince (hunt-ui.mjs:676-688), whose `git log sha..HEAD -- <globs>` can never report change for a non-existent path, so ledger expiry keyed on frontend sheet code never fires. No guard: the only persona validation (hunt-ui.mjs:137) checks merely that codeScope is a non-empty array, never that the globs resolve. The finding slightly overstates "half the surface" — packages/sheets/src/** does cover the real grid/formula/view engine — but the frontend wrapper layer the briefs drive is genuinely unreachable, which is a real scope/spec-fit defect, refutable on no named ground.

verdict.reason: Verified in the working tree. `cmdRun` accepts `--fault` (hunt-ui.mjs:35, 802) and threads it into `runHunt` (839); `runHunt` marks a seeded run only via `console.error` (922-924) and otherwise branches on `fault` solely to pass it to the session/replay (307, 1023-1024). All artifacts are written unconditionally to the normal outDir and ledger (842-864): `renderUiReport` has no fault parameter or field (514-577) and `run.json` serializes only `{runId, headSha, stats, reported, dropped, skipped}` (855). A fault-run finding is recorded in the shared novelty ledger as `verdict: "reported"` under `fp: dk` (1104), where the key (994, uiDefectKey) carries persona/action/reader/operator/ground and no fault component, so it shares a key space with genuine ground-A findings and can suppress them. This contradicts the feature's own stated rule at packages/frontend/src/app/harness/hunt/page.tsx:75-79 ("published as data-hunt-harness-fault … so a seeded run can never be mistaken for a real one"), which is only consumed by verify-hunt-oracles.mjs:298,307 — the path docs/design/harness-engineering.md:1990-2004 describes as the positive control; the end-to-end `run --fault` path is additional surface with no ledger/output separation. No guard elsewhere makes it unreachable (hunt-ui-session.mjs:96-118 wires it fully). This is an approach/design-fit violation, in-lane and blocking-kind; I found no ground to refute.
